newsitem.title: USA: NHL-LECLAIR SCORES TWICE AS HEXTALL AND FLYERS BLANK CAPITALS.
newsitem.headline: NHL-LECLAIR SCORES TWICE AS HEXTALL AND FLYERS BLANK CAPITALS.

text.p: Ron Hextall faced only 15 shots but stopped them all and John LeClair scored twice as the Philadelphia Flyers blanked the Washington Capitals 5-0 on Sunday.
Eric Lindros had four assists and Rod Brind'Amour, Eric Desjardins and Colin Forbes also scored for the Flyers, who outshot the Caps 25-15, including 13-2 in the second period.
Hextall, who was coming back from a hamstring strain, notched his fourth shutout of the season and 18th of his career by shutting the door on Washington.
Brind'Amour's 22nd goal of the season with 3:36 left in the first period gave Hextall all the offence he would need.
The Flyers led 3-0 after two periods. LeClair snuffed any chance of a Washington comeback by beating Bill Ranford twice in the third, notching his 43rd and 44th goals of the season.
"Our guys did a real good job today, played a really good defensive game," Hextall said. "We didn't give up a whole lot of rushes ... we played a real solid game."
The Flyers' penalty killing unit was especially sharp as the Caps went 0-for-5 with a man advantage.
In San Jose, Mike Richter made 28 saves and Niklas Sundstrom scored the go-ahead goal late in the second period as the New York Rangers held on for a 2-1 win over the Sharks.
Luc Robitaille also scored for New York, with Wayne Gretzky assisting on both goals.

Jeff Friesen's powerplay goal with two minutes left in the first period tied the game for San Jose. Sundstrom scored his 22nd of the season with five minutes left in the second period to break the deadlock.
The Rangers were outshot 11-2 in the third, but Richter was able to preserve the lead with several key saves.
In Buffalo, Dave Andreychuk had a goal and an assist and John MacLean set up two goals as the New Jersey Devils ended the Sabres' 11-game home unbeaten streak with a 4-1 victory.
Steve Thomas, Denis Pederson and Valeri Zelepukin scored for New Jersey in a three-goal second period. Dixon Ward's goal for Buffalo at 2:02 of the third spoiled Martin Brodeur's shutout bid.
Andreychuk's empty-net tally with 58 seconds left was career goal number 499 for the long-time former Sabre.
At Tampa Bay, Rob Zamunmer tallied 2:20 into overtime to give the Lightning a 2-1 victory over the Calgary Flames.
Cory Cross gathered in a lose puck and sent it toward Zamuner, who re-directed it into the open right side of the Calgary net for the game-winner.
Roman Hamrlik scored a powerplay goal at 9:18 of the second period for Tampa Bay. Jonas Hoglund tied the game with 7:43 left in the third.
Corey Schwab finished with 44 saves for Tampa Bay, which is 8-3-1 in its last 12 games.
In St Louis, Mike Grier and Doug Weight each had two goals and an assist and Curtis Joseph made 26 saves against his former team as the Edmonton Oilers beat the Blues 4-1.
It was the first career two-goal game for Grier, who has six goals in his last six games.
Pierre Turgeon scored the only goal for the Blues, who have lost five in a row.

At Colorado, Teemu Selanne scored a powerplay goal with 3:18 left in regulation and the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim extended their unbeaten streak to a team-record eight games by rallying for a 2-2 tie with the Avalanche.
The Ducks, 6-0-2 in their last eight, were enjoying a two-man advantage when Selanne got the puck and banked a shot off goaltender Patrick Roy for his 42nd goal of the season.
Paul Kariya scored the first Anaheim goal just eight seconds into the game when he grabbed a loose puck off the opening faceoff and fired a shot through Roy's pads.
Peter Forsberg and Adam Deadmarsh scored for Colorado.
At Florida, Tim Sweeney scored twice and Jim Carey made 26 saves to lead the Boston Bruins to a 3-1 victory over the struggling Panthers.
Bob Beers's powerplay goal at 7:43 of the second period gave Boston a 1-0 lead and Sweeney doubled the advantage with an unassisted tally at at 5:51 of the third.
Steve Washburn's first NHL goal on a powerplay at 9:35 of the third was the only shot to get past Carey as the Panthers fell to 1-8-2 in their last 11 games.
